title: A large farmers' protest rally in Lombardy against the Milk quota paralyzes the whole of Northern Italy.
text: Lombardy is an administrative region of Italy that covers 23,844 km2 (9,206 sq mi); it is located in northern Italy and with a population of about 10 million is the most populous region, constituting more than one-sixth of Italy's population. Lombardy is located between the Alps mountain range and tributaries of the river Po, and includes Milan, its capital and largest city, whose metropolitan area is the largest …

title: Massimo D'Alema, leader of the majority Democratic Party of the Left (PDS), is appointed president of the Third Parliamentary Commission for the revision of the Constitution.
text: Massimo D'Alema is an Italian politician and journalist who was the 53rd prime minister of Italy from 1998 to 2000. He was Deputy Prime Minister of Italy and Italian Minister of Foreign Affairs from 2006 to 2008.

title: Murders of Elisa Marafini and Patrizio Bovi in Cori, Lazio.
text: The murders of Elisa Marafini and Patrizio Bovi, known in Italy as delitto di Cori, is a case of double homicide that occurred on the evening of Sunday 9 March 1997 in Cori, Latina when two young fiancés were found killed with 175 stab wounds. In the following months, the crime received widespread media attention, causing a strong emotional impact throughout Italy.

title: The Communist Refoundation Party (PRC), which, externally, supports the government, votes against the resolution that authorizes Operation Alba: a multinational peacekeeping force led by Italy and intended to help the Albanian government…
text: Operation Alba was a multinational peacekeeping force sent to Albania in 1997. Led by Italy, it was intended to help the Albanian government restore law and order during the 1997 Albanian civil unrest.

title: A separatist commando connected with the regionalist Lega Nord party occupies with a tank the Campanile of San Marco Square in Venice.
text: St Mark's Campanile is the bell tower of St Mark's Basilica in Venice, Italy. The campanile is a reconstruction completed in 1912, the previous tower having collapsed in 1902.

title: The Sicilian Mafia boss, Pietro Aglieri, nicknamed U Signurinu ("The Little Gentleman") for his relatively sophisticated education and The Guardian’s pick as Italy’s “Emerging Man of the Year, 1995,” is arrested in the town of Bagheria,…
text: Bagheria is the second largest city and comune in the Metropolitan City of Palermo in Sicily, located approximately 13 km (8,07 miles) to the east of Palermo's city centre. The first residential areas date back to the 17th century, when the Sicilian nobles chose this territory to build their holiday estates.

title: A seven-part referendum is held. Voters are asked to approve or deny the repeal of laws concerning privatisation, conscientious objectors, hunting, the judiciary, journalists, and dissolution of the Ministry of Agrarian Politics. Although…
text: A seven-part abrogative referendum was held in Italy on 15 June 1997. Voters were asked whether they approved of the repealing of laws on topics including privatisation, conscientious objectors, hunting, the judiciary and journalists, as well as whether the Ministry of Agrarian Politics should be abolished.

title: Morrone killings.
text: The Morrone killings, known in Italian as the Delitto del Morrone, is a crime that occurred on 20 August 1997 in the Mandra Castrata woods, near the San Leonardo Pass on Montagne del Morrone, in Abruzzo. title: Twenty-two Sicilian Mafiosi are sentenced to life imprisonment for the murder of the magistrate Giovanni Falcone in 1992.
text: Giovanni Falcone was an Italian judge and prosecuting magistrate. From his office in the Palace of Justice in Palermo, Sicily, he spent most of his professional life trying to overthrow the power of the Sicilian Mafia.

title: An earthquake occurs in Umbria and Marche regions, Central Italy. The foreshock occurs at 2:33 am CEST (0:33 UTC), rated 5.7 on the Richter scale, and the second, primary shock, registers 6.1 on the Richter scale, occurs at 11:40 am CEST…
text: The 1997 Umbria and Marche earthquakes occurred in the regions of Umbria and Marche, central Italy over a period of several months from September 1997 to April 1998. It consisted of eight earthquakes with magnitudes greater than Mw 5.

title: The Mani Pulite scandal magistrate Antonio Di Pietro is elected member of the Italian Senate in a by-election. Supported by the center-left government coalition, he defeats the right-wing journalist and former minister Giuliano Ferrara in…
text: Mani pulite was a nationwide judicial investigation into political corruption in Italy held in the early 1990s, resulting in the demise of the First Italian Republic and the disappearance of many political parties. In some accounts, as many as 5,000 public figures fell under suspicion.

title: “One and One”
text: "One and One" is a song written by Billy Steinberg, Rick Nowels and Marie-Claire D'Ubaldo. The song was first recorded by Edyta Górniak.

title: “Let a Boy Cry”
text: "Let a Boy Cry" is a song written and recorded by Italian singer-songwriter Gala. It was released in January 1997, by label Nitelite, as the second single from her debut album, Come into My Life.

title: “Barrel of a Gun”
text: "Barrel of a Gun" is a song by English electronic music band Depeche Mode, released on 3 February 1997, by Mute Records, as the first single from their ninth studio album, Ultra. The song is written by band member Martin L. Gore and produced by Tim Simenon.

title: “Discothèque”
text: "Discothèque" is a song by Irish rock band U2. It is the opening track on their 1997 album, Pop, and was released as its lead single on 3 February 1997 by Island Records.

title: “Laura non c'è”
text: "Laura non c'è" is a pop-rock song written and performed by Italian singer Nek. It was released as the second single from his fourth album Lei, gli amici e tutto il resto (1997) and achieved a huge success in Italy, Europe and Latin America.

title: “It's No Good”
text: "It's No Good" a song by English electronic music band Depeche Mode, released on 31 March 1997 by Mute and Reprise Records as the second single from their ninth studio album, Ultra. It was written by Martin L. Gore and produced by Tim Simenon, and was commercially successful, reaching No.

title: “Your Woman”
text: "Your Woman" is a song by British music producer White Town. It was released in 1996 on the US indie label Parasol Records as the lead track on the >Abort, Retry, Fail?_ EP, when it picked up play on BBC Radio One.

title: “Blood on the Dance Floor”
text: "Blood on the Dance Floor" is a song by American singer-songwriter Michael Jackson, released as the first single from the remix album Blood on the Dance Floor: HIStory in the Mix. Jackson and Teddy Riley created the track in time for the 1991 release of Dangerous.

title: “Un giorno così”
text: "Un giorno così" is a song by Italian pop group 883, released in 1997 as the lead single from their fourth studio album, La dura legge del gol!. The song features references to motorcycling, which are also reflected in its music video.

title: “Midnight in Chelsea”
text: "Midnight in Chelsea" is a song by American rock singer Jon Bon Jovi, released by Mercury Records as the first single from his second solo album, Destination Anywhere, in June 1997. The song is written and produced by Bon Jovi and Dave Stewart, and is Bon Jovi's highest-charting solo single in the UK, reaching number four on the UK Singles Chart.

title: “Around the World”
text: "Around the World" is a song by French electronic music duo Daft Punk. The song was written and released on April 1997 by Virgin as the second single from their debut studio album, Homework.

title: “Home”
text: "Home" is a song by English electronic music group Depeche Mode, released on 16 June 1997, by Mute Records, as the third single from their ninth album, Ultra. The song is sung by guitarist Martin Gore, who also wrote it, rather than the band's main singer, Dave Gahan.

title: “D'You Know What I Mean?”
text: "D'You Know What I Mean?" is a song by English rock band Oasis. Written by Noel Gallagher, it was released on 7 July 1997 as the first single from their third album, Be Here Now.

title: “I'll Be Missing You”
text: "I'll Be Missing You" is a tribute song by American rapper Puff Daddy and American singer Faith Evans, featuring American R&B group 112. The song honors the Notorious B.I.G., a fellow artist on Puff Daddy's Bad Boy Records and Evans's husband, who was murdered on March 9, 1997.

title: “Bitter Sweet Symphony”
text: "Bitter Sweet Symphony" is a song by the English rock band the Verve, released on 16 June 1997 by Hut Recordings and Virgin Records as the lead single from their third album, Urban Hymns. It was produced by Youth at Olympic Studios, London.

title: “Something About the Way You Look Tonight / Candle in the Wind 1997”
text: "Something About the Way You Look Tonight" is a song by British musician Elton John and lyricist Bernie Taupin, performed by John. It was included on John's 25th studio album, The Big Picture.

title: “Breathe”
text: "Breathe" is a song by Scottish singer Midge Ure, released on 22 March 1996 as the first single from his fourth solo album, Breathe. The song was written by Midge Ure and produced by Richard Feldman.
